extracted.intended_audience: taxpayers, tax practitioners, promoters, pass-through entities, qualified organizations, and material advisors involved in syndicated conservation easement transactions
extracted.subtask_description: Final Treasury/IRS regulatory guidance for identifying, measuring, and reporting syndicated conservation easement listed transactions, covering definitions, timing rules, methods to determine an investor's investment (anti-stuffing and relevant-basis), the role of promotional materials, participant/material-advisor rules, and reporting burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-stuffing method — measure of taxpayer's investment
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the anti-stuffing method, the amount of a taxpayer's investment in the pass-through entity is the portion of the cash and fair market value of the assets the taxpayer uses to acquire its interest in the pass-through entity that is attributable to the real property on which a conservation easement is placed (or the portion thereof) and that produces the charitable contribution deduction described in § 1.6011-9(b)(3). If an investor uses non-cash assets to acquire its interest, the fair market value (not basis) of such assets is the relevant measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies even where pass-through entity owns cash and marketable securities in addition to real property; requires allocation of acquisition cost to property giving rise to the deduction. Treasury/IRS view is that parties will have considered allocation in promotional materials, so the calculation is not unduly burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant-basis alternative method for amount of investment
rubrics_metrics.description: For contributions occurring on or after December 30, 2022, taxpayers may elect to use their relevant basis, as determined under section 170(h)(7)(B) and its regulations, as the amount of their investment for purposes of § 1.6011-9(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This alternative reduces duplicative calculations for partnerships and S corporations that must calculate relevant basis for section 170(f)(19) and investors who must calculate investment under listed-transaction rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of investment measurement — amounts after contribution excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: The anti-stuffing method focuses on amounts invested in the property giving rise to the deduction as of the time of the charitable contribution; amounts expended on the property after the contribution (e.g., later rehabilitation, maintenance, property taxes) are not part of the taxpayer's investment for the anti-stuffing calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treasury/IRS rejected treating post-contribution cash 'earmarked' for future expenditures as attributable to the contributed property because such a rule would be difficult to administer and require fact-intensive projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assets retained for future operation/maintenance not attributable
rubrics_metrics.description: Assets retained to pay for costs related to operation and maintenance of the real property on which the conservation easement is placed, including costs that may be incurred in future years, are not attributable to the contributed real property for purposes of the anti-stuffing calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarified in § 1.6011-9(d)(4)(ii); excludes cash held for future taxes, repairs, or other post-contribution expenditures from the investment numerator.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.5-times ratio as element of listed transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: One element of the syndicated conservation easement listed transaction is that promotional materials offer investors the possibility of being allocated a charitable contribution deduction the amount of which equals or exceeds an amount that is two and one-half times the amount of the taxpayer's investment in the partnership (the '2.5 times' rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting the 2.5-times rule is an element illustrating tax avoidance; if met (and other elements satisfied), the transaction is a listed transaction. Quantity of promotional materials alone does not determine whether the 2.5-times rule is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of steps irrelevant (timing of pass-through acquisition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The order in which the steps of a syndicated conservation easement transaction occur is not relevant; acquiring an interest in the pass-through before it acquires real property still falls within the definition of a syndicated conservation easement transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations make explicit that the transaction falls within § 1.6011-9(b)(2) 'regardless of the order' of the steps; an example illustrates anti-stuffing when pass-through acquires property after investor invests.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exception for long-term holding periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not provide an exception from disclosure or listed-transaction status based solely on long-term holding periods of property or investor interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holding period is one element of a fact-intensive inquiry into overvaluation, and crafting a holding-period-based exception would be over- or under-inclusive. The exception in section 170(h)(7)(C) does not necessitate a similar exception here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — charitable contribution deduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined as 'a deduction under section 170 of the Internal Revenue Code (Code), which includes a deduction arising from a qualified conservation contribution as defined in section 170(h)(1).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treasury/IRS declined to limit the definition strictly to qualified conservation contributions because substantially similar transactions may involve other real property contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — conservation easement
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined to track section 170(h): a restriction (granted in perpetuity) on the use that may be made of the real property, within the meaning of section 170(h)(2)(C), exclusively for conservation purposes within the meaning of section 170(h)(1)(C) and (h)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether the taxpayer treats the contribution as a conservation easement and claims a deduction triggers listed-transaction treatment irrespective of later IRS assertions that the easement is invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — participant (who must report)
rubrics_metrics.description: A taxpayer 'participating' in a syndicated conservation easement transaction includes (1) an owner of a pass-through entity, (2) a pass-through entity (any tier), and (3) any other taxpayer whose tax return reflects tax consequences or a tax strategy arising from the syndicated conservation easement transaction. A qualified organization to which the easement is donated is not treated as a participant under § 1.6011-4(c)(3)(i)(A) for the listed transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations clarify that participants include those in transactions that are the same as or substantially similar to syndicated conservation easement transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — promotional materials (broad scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotional materials include materials described in § 301.6112-1(b)(3)(iii)(B) and any other written or oral communication regarding the transaction provided to investors, such as marketing materials, appraisals (preliminary/draft/attached to return), websites, transactional documents (deed of conveyance), private placement memoranda, tax opinions, operating agreements, subscription agreements, statements of anticipated value of the easement, and statements of the anticipated charitable contribution deduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treasury/IRS adopted a broad definition despite concerns that it is overbroad; receipt by one investor is circumstantial evidence for others but does not automatically establish receipt by all. Broad scope is warranted to prevent promoters from evading elements of the listed transaction by using oral communications or websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotional materials as an element of tax-avoidance identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The existence of promotional materials offering the possibility of a charitable contribution deduction equal to or exceeding 2.5 times the investor's investment is an important attribute illustrating tax avoidance and is an element of the listed transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if promotional materials exist, the 2.5-times threshold and other elements must be satisfied; the promotional materials requirement is not redundant with section 170(h)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Material advisor — definition and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: A person is a material advisor if the person (1) provides material aid, assistance, or advice with respect to organizing, managing, promoting, selling, implementing, insuring, or carrying out any reportable transaction, and (2) directly or indirectly derives gross income in excess of the threshold amount defined in § 301.6011-3(b)(3) for that aid. A 'tax statement' is any oral or written statement that relates to a tax aspect of a transaction causing it to be reportable; 'gross income' includes fees for a tax strategy or implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'fee' does not include amounts paid to a person in that person's capacity as a party to the transaction. Whether a deed of conveyance is a 'tax statement' depends on whether it contains statements relating to a tax aspect that causes the transaction to be reportable (generally it does not).

rubrics_metrics.name: Donee/qualified organization — material-advisor carveout and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualified organization acting solely in its capacity as a donee (e.g., accepting an easement, signing Form 8283 Section B, providing the contemporaneous written acknowledgement, receiving monitoring contributions used for that purpose) would not be considered a material advisor. However, if the qualified organization engages in activities that meet the material-advisor criteria (making tax statements, receiving fees above threshold for that advice), it should be subject to material-advisor rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing Form 8283 and acknowledgements and making representations regarding donee status are not tax statements under § 301.6111-3(b)(2)(ii)(A) and thus do not by themselves make the donee a material advisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 4965 carveout for qualified organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations maintain the section 4965 carveout to exclude a qualified organization from treatment as a party to a syndicated conservation easement transaction under section 4965 (consistent with Notice 2017-10), but Treasury/IRS may consider eliminating or limiting the carveout if qualified organizations continue to facilitate such transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters urged preserving the carveout to avoid discouraging qualified organizations from accepting easements; Treasury/IRS retained it for now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements and paperwork burden (Forms 8886 and 8918)
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection of information in these final regulations is reflected in Forms 8886 and 8918 (OMB control numbers 1545-1800 and 1545-0865). The requirement to maintain records to substantiate information on these forms remains unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated burden for a taxpayer required to file Form 8886: ~10 hours 16 minutes for recordkeeping, 4 hours 50 minutes for learning, and 6 hours 25 minutes for preparing and sending the form; estimated wage rate $102.08 (2022 dollars) yielding approx. $2,127 per filing. Treasury/IRS expects reporting burden to be low and economic impact minimal given the limited scope to time/manner of reporting and definitional information.
